text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; to understand the cause of these specific neurological symptoms, where exactly do you feel the weakness in your arms, and does it affect one side or both?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that description; the fact that your symptoms worsen with activity and improve with rest is highly suggestive of a muscle-related issue. Since the double vision occurs with vertical eye movements, can you tell me if you have noticed any drooping of your eyelids (ptosis)?
